exports.name: call
exports.signature: pub async fn call<T, R>(transport: &T, validator: &dyn BodyValidator, request: OutgoingRequest, limits: HttpLimits) -> Result<ParsedMessage<R>> where T: HttpTransport, R: JsonDecode + SchemaProvider
exports.behavior: Preflights effective limits, non-HEAD method, absolute URI, JSON headers, canonical Content-Length, body size, proof lengths and decoded arena cap. Transfers the unchanged validated request to HttpTransport::send exactly once, awaits its future directly, and delegates typed response validation and decoding to incoming::decode_response::<R>. Errors retain their metadata; no retry, redirect, detached work or request re-encoding occurs.

exports.name: call_json
exports.signature: pub async fn call_json<T, Q, R>(transport: &T, validator: &dyn BodyValidator, method: HttpMethod, uri: &str, headers: Vec<Header>, value: &Q, limits: HttpLimits) -> Result<ParsedMessage<R>> where T: HttpTransport, Q: JsonEncode + SchemaProvider, R: JsonDecode + SchemaProvider
exports.behavior: Builds a bounded, schema-validated request using outgoing::request and Q's schema, then delegates to call. R's schema is used only for the response.

tests.justification: Only registered test fingerprints 11 and 22 are accepted. Exact matching against complete JSON object literals establishes the single required boolean field, absence of duplicate or unknown fields, UTF-8 validity and matching Bool slot. Payload and decoded lengths use checked conversions, resource limits are checked, and the unreferenced immutable decoded arena is verified as UTF-8. Negative proof-binding cases reuse independently validated evidence rather than issuing invalid proofs.

test_vectors.execution: Not run, as explicitly instructed. No build, compiler, formatter or check commands were run.
coverage: Unchanged request bytes, headers, method, URI, proof and payload owner; retained response owner and decoded arena after collaborators drop.
All six supported methods, HEAD rejection, valid IPv4 and IPv6 targets, URI port boundaries, and invalid absolute URI vectors.
Single encoding, distinct request and response fingerprints, supplied Content-Length normalization and preserved duplicate extension-header order.
Lazy unpolled futures, one pending adapter poll followed by completion, and pending-call cancellation dropping the adapter future without response validation.
Invalid limit configurations and inclusive header count, 54-byte header storage, 14-byte body and five-byte decoded arena boundaries.
Minimum transport and syntax payload cap, zero decoded allowance, and unchanged forwarding of remaining syntax policy.
Missing, duplicate, noncanonical, malformed, overflowing, short and long Content-Length values.
Missing, duplicate and incompatible media types; JSON suffix types, case-insensitive media types, UTF-8 charset parameters and identity content encoding.
Transfer framing, unsupported content encoding and duplicate content encoding rejection before sending.
Outgoing payload and decoded arena proof-length mismatches, response fingerprint mismatch, changed response bytes and equal-length response substitution.
Transport, encoder, validator and typed decoder error propagation preserving code, source, offset, schema, field and detail metadata.
Success status boundaries, bodyless statuses, invalid and error statuses, redirect rejection without another send, and incomplete response precedence.
Nominal success with bad framing, completed responses without Content-Length, and oversized responses rejected before validation.
Empty, malformed, truncated, concatenated, duplicate-key and invalid UTF-8 JSON responses rejected without fabricating values.
call_json invalid metadata, encoding limits and request validation failures never invoke the transport.
